record.original_question: Let G be an absolutely almost simple linear algebraic group that is anisotropic over F. Does G remain anisotropic over every finite extension K/F whose degree is not divisible by any prime in the set S(G) of homological torsion primes of G?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.3. Let G be an absolutely almost simple linear algebraic group that is anisotropic over F. Does G remain anisotropic over every finite extension K/F of dimension not divisible by any prime in S(G)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $G$ be an absolutely almost simple linear algebraic group defined over $F$ (i.e. a connected linear algebraic $F$-group such that, after base change to an algebraic closure of $F$, the group becomes a simple algebraic group, with no nontrivial connected normal subgroups). Recall that $G$ is called anisotropic over $F$ if $G$ contains no nontrivial $F$-split torus, equivalently the $F$-rank of $G$ is zero.

To $G$ one associates a finite set $S(G)$ of "torsion primes" (the homological/cohomological torsion primes of $G$): these are the primes appearing in the torsion of the integral cohomology of a compact form of $G$, and they depend only on the Killing–Cartan type of $G$. Explicitly, the torsion primes are: $\{2\}$ for type $B_n,C_n,D_n$ ($n\ge 2$), $G_2$; $\{2,3\}$ for types $D_n$ ($n\ge 4$ in some conventions), $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$; and $\{2,3,5\}$ for $E_8$; together with primes dividing the order of the fundamental group when $G$ is not simply connected/adjoint as appropriate.

Question: Suppose $G$ is anisotropic over $F$. Is it true that for every finite field extension $K/F$ whose degree $[K:F]$ is not divisible by any prime in $S(G)$, the group $G$ remains anisotropic over $K$?

Related results on torsion primes and behavior of anisotropic groups under field extensions exist (Chernousov, Merkurjev, Gille and others), but no source verifying this specific question as solved was located, so the status is reported as unknown.
